== Biography ==

Ozma, also called Princess Ozma, rules the Emerald City and all four countries of Oz. Each of those countries has its own lesser ruler; by the shaggy man's account, confirmed by the boy at his side, these local rulers stand beneath Ozma much as officers stand beneath a general, with Ozma holding the highest position among them.

Ozma commands magic beyond her rank. She has brought Dorothy over to Oz on her Magic Carpet, one of the means, alongside the Nome King's Magic Belt, by which Dorothy has reached the Emerald City.

== Narrative role ==

Ozma's part in the story centers on her authority as ruler of Oz. The Cowardly Lion and the Hungry Tiger meet the traveling party with Ozma's golden chariot and escort them into the Emerald City and into the royal palace. Later, Ozma's birthday celebration draws many guests to the palace and its grounds; once the festivities end, the [[Wizard]] sends several of the visitors home in magic bubbles, while Dorothy returns to Kansas by the Magic Belt.

== Personality ==

Ozma's authority is described as comprehensive yet layered: she "rules the Emerald City and all the four countries of Oz," while each country retains its own lesser ruler beneath her — an arrangement likened to an army, where "the little rulers are all captains, and Ozma's the general." This framing casts her as a sovereign who holds overall command without displacing the local governance beneath her, suggesting a disposition toward structured, delegated rule rather than direct micromanagement of every territory.

Consistent with this standing, she is said to have welcomed a visitor to Oz "in gracious accents" as "the girl Ruler" — a detail suggesting a courteous, dignified bearing toward those entering her domain, in keeping with her position as its foremost authority.

== Powers ==

Ozma commands magic beyond her own person: her Magic Carpet can carry a traveler across vast distances in an instant, as when it brought a companion back to the Emerald City after other magic had failed. Her authority extends over the Emerald City and all four countries of Oz, each governed by a lesser ruler who answers to her — as captains answer to a general.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Dorothy]]''' — friend. Dorothy recalls that "Ozma took me over on her Magic Carpet," suggesting a bond of trust and assistance between the two.

'''[[Jellia Jamb]]''' — employment. Jellia Jamb is described as "Ozma's favorite attendant," which could indicate a relationship of service within Ozma's household.

'''[[Santa Claus]]''' — friend. An account holds that "Ozma invited me and I just couldn't help coming to celebrate the happy occasion," hinting at a friendly rapport extending an invitation from Ozma.

'''[[Jack Pumpkinhead]]''' — family. Jack Pumpkinhead states, "Ozma's my parent, you know, because she built my body and carved my pumpkin head," a claim that suggests a parental bond, though it rests on Jack Pumpkinhead's own framing of his creation.

'''[[THE shaggy man]]''' — acquaintance. Ozma greets him with "You are welcome to Oz," spoken "in gracious accents," suggesting a cordial but formal acquaintance befitting her position as ruler.

== Trivia ==

* Ozma once carried Dorothy across on her Magic Carpet, one of several magical means — alongside the Silver Shoes and the Nome King's Magic Belt — that have moved Dorothy between worlds.
* Although Ozma rules the Emerald City and all four countries of Oz, each country keeps its own smaller ruler; the shaggy man compares this arrangement to a military hierarchy, with the four rulers as captains and Ozma as the general.
